content.title: About
content.content: French toast is a dish made from slices of bread soaked in a mixture of eggs, milk, and spices, then fried until golden brown. It is often served with syrup, berries, powdered sugar, or butter. In fast‑food restaurants it is prepared quickly using pre‑mixed batters and pre‑sliced bread.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in France in the 17th century but became popular in the United States in the early 20th century.
Traditional recipes include cinnamon and vanilla, while modern versions may add banana, chocolate, or nuts.
French toast is commonly served for breakfast but can also appear on lunch and dinner menus.
In some countries it is called “egg toast” or “golden toast.”
Fast preparation is achieved by using ready‑made egg‑milk mixes.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Eggs provide complete protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Milk and occasional cheese add calcium important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and milk are rich in B2, B6, and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Carbohydrates from the bread supply quick energy, useful for active people.

items.title: Antioxidants in spices
items.content: Cinnamon and vanilla contain polyphenols with antioxidant properties.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Butter and syrup can significantly increase the dish’s calorie count.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Added sweeteners may be problematic for people with diabetes.

items.title: Egg or milk allergy
items.content: Individuals with food allergies may react to these ingredients.

items.title: Gluten in bread
items.content: Traditional bread contains gluten, making the dish unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve French toast hot, drizzled with maple syrup, fruit sauce, or dusted with powdered sugar. It can be topped with fresh fruit, nuts, yogurt, or bacon for a more filling option.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared French toast is best eaten immediately. If needed, cool it in an airtight container for up to 2 days and reheat in an oven or toaster. Do not keep it longer than 3 days to avoid loss of flavor and texture.
